messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 Alert fired for customer Acme Corp (cust-1123): Private control plane unreachable in us-west-2 (vpc-0a1b2c3d). Auto-page to oncall.
pagerduty: Incident  INC-2026-0421 created and notified: P1 - private-control-plane-unreachable-cust-1123.
mike (oncall): acked :hand: I'm on it, taking lead. Starting triage — informing CS and network.
emily (cs): Thanks Mike. Acme reports all model endpoints returning 504/timeouts since ~03:12 UTC. They say it's affecting production traffic only.
jordan (sre): quick checks: control-plane pods show "NotReady" on the private cluster. Agent heartbeats missing for that customer. running initial k8s describe now.
jordan (sre): paste: ```kubectl get pods -n acme-controlplane -o wide
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
controlplane-0                          0/1     CrashLoop 4          2h
controlplane-1                          1/1     Running   0          2h
controlplane-2                          0/1     CrashLoop 3          2h
```
rajesh (network): I see BGP sessions from customer vgw to our transit gone for that VPC around 03:11 UTC. Possible upstream flapping or route leak. Pulling flow logs.
acme-support: Confirmed — we saw a routing flap around 03:10-03:14, lots of timeouts. Our on-prem team says nothing changed on their side at that time.
jordan (sre): trying to exec into controlplane-1 to check agent manager logs. ``kubectl logs controlplane-1 -n acme-controlplane``
jordan (sre): tail shows repeated TLS handshake failures when reaching customer agent: "x509: certificate is valid for lefty, not acme-agent" — hmm cert mismatch.
mike (oncall): summarize impact: customer control plane partially degraded -> requests to private endpoints 50-100% failures depending on shard. Marking impact: Production partial outage for Acme. Emily, can you draft customer-facing blurb for status page? Keep it factual and avoid speculation.
emily (cs): Drafting: "We are investigating connectivity issues affecting Acme Corp's private control plane in us-west-2 causing timeouts to model endpoints. Our engineers are actively investigating." Will post once we have mitigation.
rajesh (network): I'm rerunning BGP neigh show and pulling route tables. If BGP is down and certs also failing, could be control plane cert rotation collided with agent restart and BGP flapped during that window. Checking timestamps.
sara (secondary-oncall): If certs are the issue, can we fallback to hosted control plane for this customer while we remediate? Need approval from product/security to route traffic — might be cross-tenant implications.
mike (oncall): good idea. Jordan, what would it take to fail traffic to hosted fallback? Any quick toggle?
jordan (sre): We have a routing policy to fallback to hosted-bridge for private customers in emergencies. Command below to trigger (dry-run first):
```
# promote fallback route for cust-1123
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --customer cust-1123 --to hosted-bridge --dry-run
# if OK, remove --dry-run
```
jordan (sre): Dry-run shows no conflicts. If we flip, sessions will route through hosted control plane and bypass customer agent/VPC. Expected latency increase ~30-80ms for embeddings, but restores connectivity.
mike (oncall): proceed with fallback toggle after CS approves messaging. Emily, have Acme OK with fallback?
emily (cs): messaging sent to Acme support channel asking for permission; they responded "we authorize temporary hosted fallback to restore production traffic". They asked to be notified of any key rotation.
jordan (sre): executing fallback now, switching route for cust-1123 -> hosted-bridge. Running command without --dry-run.
incident-bot: action-log: redwoodctl routing set-fallback --customer cust-1123 --to hosted-bridge executed by jordan at 1785006845.
jordan (sre): flip completed. Verifying agent connections...
rajesh (network): BGP still showing intermittent drops, but traffic to hosted bridge now sees successful TLS handshakes.
acme-support: Observed traffic recovery — endpoints responding at ~03:15 UTC. Some increased latency but functional.
mike (oncall): good. Marking mitigation: temporary hosted fallback enabled. Next steps: fix root cause — looks like cert rotation mismatch plus BGP instability. Jordan to collect logs and cert timeline, Rajesh to coordinate with cloud provider on BGP flaps, CS to coordinate customer comms and make sure they accept hosted fallback duration.
jordan (sre): collecting cert rotation logs and agent update history. Paste from cert manager: ```
2026-03-14T03:08:02Z cert-rotator: issued new cert acme-agent-2026-03-14
2026-03-14T03:09:50Z cert-rotator: started rolling restart of agent pods
2026-03-14T03:10:55Z agent-manager: restarted agent, attempted handshake with cert acme-agent-2026-03-14, remote presented old cert -> handshake failed
```
rajesh (network): opened ticket with cloud-provider support: CP-98765. Provided BGP logs and timestamps. Asking for jitter/maintenance window checks.
emily (cs): Posted initial status update to customer and internal status page: "Acme production connectivity restored via hosted fallback. Root cause investigation ongoing. Expecting follow-up in 60 minutes." cc @acme-support
acme-support: Thanks team. Please keep us updated. We will monitor and escalate internally if anything else.
sara (secondary-oncall): handoff note for next oncall (overnight): fallback enabled for cust-1123; mitigation stable as of 1785006900. Ongoing actions: collect cert rotator logs, coordinate provider on BGP, decide permanent rollback or cert reissue.
mike (oncall): agreed. I'll remain primary until confirmed root cause. If alerts quiet and logs collected, we'll change severity to P2 in 90m. For now keeping P1.
incident-bot: pagerduty update: Incident INC-2026-0421 acknowledged by mike. Status: mitigation in place.
jordan (sre): attaching collected artifacts (links internal): /artifacts/INC-2026-0421/—cert-logs, bgp-flows, controlplane-pod-logs. (links posted in thread)
rajesh (network): follow-up: cloud provider indicates no scheduled maintenance; they are investigating edge flaps. We may need to propose a BGP hold-time change if jitter continues.
emily (cs): will send customer the postmortem ETA once we have timeline. For now they've accepted the fallback and will notify when they want to revert.
mike (oncall): closing loop: action items assigned -> jordan (dive into cert rotator + reissue plan), rajesh (cloud BGP troubleshooting + provider ticket), emily (customer comms), sara (overnight oncall). If anyone else sees related alerts, ping this thread.
acme-support: Thank you all, team. Appreciated quick restore.
mike (oncall): logging final note: mitigation confirmed as of 1785006900; will monitor for 2 hours. If stable, change to P2 and start postmortem. :white_check_mark:
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for incident coordination. Conforms to agents.md rules: single continuous string, messages prefixed by sender, includes bot messages, ack, escalation, handoff, customer impact, mitigation, logs and commands. All fields are flat strings or arrays of strings.
